logline: A 12-year-old boy navigates the beautiful friction of a middle-class Jaipur family in 1998 - a nostalgia-precise love letter to Indian childhoods on the cusp of the cable TV era.

renewal.note: Four seasons completed. Season 4 released August 2024. No Season 5 announced as of June 2026.

bollymeter.basis: Individual Season 1 episode IMDb ratings reach 9.1 and 9.4 - among the highest for any Indian web series; Firstpost praised its ordinary brilliance and Scroll.in credited it with capturing the essence of 1990s India on the cusp of economic and cultural change.

pull_quotes.text: Yeh Meri Family may surprise audiences with its ordinary brilliance.

seasons.review_body: Yeh Meri Family premiered on TVFPlay and YouTube on July 12, 2018 - seven episodes set entirely within a Jaipur household in 1998, narrated from the perspective of 12-year-old Harshu Gupta. Creator Sameer Saxena built the season around the precise emotional texture of a pre-liberalization Indian middle-class family: the arrival of cable TV as a domestic battleground, the specific indignities of being the youngest child, the way parents' ambitions for their children and their own unsatisfied desires coexist in a two-bedroom flat. IMDb episode ratings for Season 1 peak at 9.4 and 9.1 - among the highest episode-level scores for any Indian web series. Firstpost called it an exercise in ordinary brilliance, and Scroll.in credited it with capturing 1990s India's cultural transition with more specificity than its budget suggested was possible. Mona Singh's mother role is the anchor the child performances orbit around.

episode_reviews.title: Chiddiya Ud
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 1 finale is the highest-rated episode of the entire series on IMDb. It earns its emotional weight through accumulation - seven episodes of precise family observation pay off in a conclusion that does not manufacture drama but simply renders a family moment at its most honest.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A scene in which the family's usual noise drops into something quieter - the kind of beat Indian TV had long treated as insufficient, but this show had been training its audience to receive.

episode_reviews.title: The 12th Man
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The cricket episode captures the 1998 World Cup fever that organized Indian summers before satellite news colonized the living room. The family dynamics play out through the show's most shared cultural reference point of the season.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Harshu's negotiation of loyalties between a cricket match and a family obligation - a small compromise that feels enormous at twelve.

bollymeter.basis: The show shifts its lead to teenage protagonist Ritika for Seasons 2-4, a structural reset that changes the emotional register; episode IMDb ratings for Season 2 are strong but the singular nostalgic intensity of Season 1 is not replicated.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in May 2023 on Amazon Prime Video, five years after the first season and with a structural change: the show shifted its central perspective from Harshu Gupta (Season 1) to teenager Ritika Awasthi, effectively beginning a new coming-of-age arc within a new family. Mona Singh and Akarsh Khurana returned but with their characters repositioned. The reset allowed TVF to continue the nostalgic family-drama format while escaping the challenge of aging the original child cast. Audience reception was warm and IMDb scores held above the general Indian web series baseline, though the episodic intensity that made Season 1 individual episodes score in the 9s did not return.
seasons.season_over_season: Structural reset: new protagonist Ritika replaces Harshu, new family unit, Amazon Prime Video distribution; the 90s nostalgia frame widens to accommodate 2000s India.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 maintains the show's warm register with episode IMDb ratings in the 8.4 range; steady output without the breakthrough moments that defined Season 1.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 continued the Ritika arc in April 2024, with the show now a reliably warm presence on Amazon Prime Video rather than a cultural event. Individual episode ratings settle consistently in the 8.4 range on IMDb - well above average, but reflecting an audience that has adapted its expectations to a comfort-watch mode rather than the arrested-attention mode of Season 1. The five-episode run is efficiently paced and the family dynamics remain specific enough to avoid generic sitcom territory.
seasons.season_over_season: Consistent continuation of the Ritika arc; episode quality steady, cultural impact has normalized from Season 1's peak.

bollymeter.basis: Episode IMDb ratings for Season 4 return to the 8.4-8.8 range, a slight uptick from Season 3; the Independence Day episode scoring 8.8 suggests the show found a thematic groove again in its final season.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 in August 2024 appears to be the series' concluding chapter, with TVF having not announced a fifth season. The five-episode run closes the Ritika arc with episode-level IMDb scores ticking back up toward the 8.8 range - notably the Independence Day episode, which uses the historical setting that TVF handles well, returned to the kind of specific cultural observation that made Season 1 essential. The show ends as a complete four-season coming-of-age chronicle rather than trailing off, which is the correct way for a TVF family series to conclude.
seasons.season_over_season: Final season returns to stronger episode scores; closes the series with cultural specificity rather than formula.
